label: NOTE: FPM_PPS_filter is 753 bytes of geometry -- a circular history, a strided coefficient walk, two rails truncated separately, and a phase that consumes a symbol when it wraps. Every mutation here moves one of those and nothing else.
the coefficient stride is the tap count rather than the phase count, which is the V.22 block's permuted layout applied to this one
the second run of the rail includes hist[widx] again instead of stopping above it
the second run starts at the top of the buffer rather than one below it
the rail's accumulator is shifted down by fourteen instead of fifteen
the rail walks the history forwards instead of newest first
the mapped source takes the whole ring entry as an index rather than its low byte
the mapped source reads the map with the write cursor instead of the read cursor
the two rails of the direct source are transposed
the two constellation maps are transposed
the mapped and direct forms are chosen the other way round
the read cursor wraps at one short of the ring length
the write cursor wraps at one short of the tap count
the symbol is stored before the write cursor advances rather than after
the count is decremented by one rather than by the debt it just paid
the two rails are differenced the other way round
the rails are summed instead of differenced, which drops the carrier's quadrature term
the difference is not truncated to sixteen bits before the output gain
the output gain is applied without its shift
the phase advances by the nominal step alone, dropping the timing correction
the phase wraps one step late
the wrap resets the phase instead of subtracting the phase count, so the fractional part is lost
the wrap does not ask for the next symbol
the debt is left standing rather than cleared before the phase test
the read cursor is not written back, so a caller feeding one ring across calls re-sends the same symbols
the phase is not carried across calls
the two histories are transposed at the store
both rails are filtered with the I coefficients
the rails are filtered at the phase the NEXT output will use
find:
yi = pps_rail(state->hist_i, state->cfg.coeff_i, phases, phase,
			      taps, widx);
replace:
yi = pps_rail(state->hist_i, state->cfg.coeff_i, phases,
			      (short)(phase + step), taps, widx);

label: NOTE: FPM_PPS_init and FPM_PPS_free are allocation and release, so the mutations below are measured with the allocator's books -- counts, request sizes and null releases -- and not by reading freed memory.
the reuse test decides on the COEFFICIENT COUNT rather than on the quotient it sizes the buffers with, which is FPM_SRE_init's shape and the slip deviation D400 records
the reuse test also reallocates when the tap count is unchanged
a re-init always reallocates, so there is no reuse path at all
the realloc path forgets to ask for new buffers, leaving the two pointers dangling
the tap count divides by the phase count plus one
the tap count divides by the phase STEP rather than the phase count
the histories are sized in ENTRIES rather than in bytes, so each is half the size it must be
the histories are V.22's 2 * taps entries rather than this block's taps
only one history is allocated
`phase` is seeded from zero rather than from the nominal step
`need` starts at one, as FPM_SRE_init's counterpart does, so the first output takes a symbol first
`widx` is not reset by a re-init
the clear loop stops one short of the tap count
the clear loop runs to the tap count the buffers were ALLOCATED with rather than the new one, which on the shrinking reuse path writes past the new length
only the in-phase history is cleared
FPM_PPS_free releases only the in-phase history
FPM_PPS_free releases the in-phase history twice

FPM_PPS_free releases the two histories the other way round.  SURVIVOR, and it cannot be otherwise: `sysdep_free` has no ordering effect a caller can observe, both releases happen unconditionally, and nothing allocates afterwards -- so the allocator's books are identical under either order.  The object's order (hist_q first, at 0x0a9898 before 0x0a98a3) is reproduced because the object encodes it, not because a test can see it.

init's realloc path releases the two histories the other way round.  SURVIVOR for the same reason as the pair in FPM_PPS_free: two unconditional releases with nothing between them, and the two allocations that follow are recorded by count and by request size, neither of which an order can move.

the tap count is derived from the CALLER's configuration rather than from the copy init just made.  SURVIVOR, and unreachable rather than untested: the two objects hold the same ten dwords by the time this line runs, so they can only disagree if `cfg` aliases `state->cfg` -- that is, if a caller passes the state's own configuration back into init, which is a self-assignment no caller can want and none is reconstructed.  The object reads the COPY (`movswl 0x20(%ebx)` and `movswl (%ebx)`, both off the state pointer, not off `cfg`), so that is what is written.

the two byte counts are truncated to sixteen bits, as FPM_SRE_init's are.  SURVIVOR by arithmetic: it can only change a value when `2 * taps` exceeds 32767, i.e. above 16384 taps, which needs `cfg.coeffs` above 163840 with ten phases -- and `cfg.coeffs` is a short. UNREACHABLE THROUGH THE FIELD'S OWN TYPE. The object does not encode the truncation (`lea (%esi,%esi,1)` and `add %esi,%esi` on a sign-extended 32-bit tap count, no `cwtl`, no 16-bit store), which is a measured difference from the sibling and is why the plain form is written.
find:
state->hist_i = sysdep_malloc(2 * state->taps);
		state->hist_q = sysdep_malloc(2 * state->taps);
replace:
state->hist_i = sysdep_malloc((short)(2 * state->taps));
		state->hist_q = sysdep_malloc((short)(2 * state->taps));
